trust_decision.summary: The app decides a caller's org/space identity from a client certificate that ASP.NET certificate forwarding takes from a request header (default or caller-chosen name), so the app never sees proof that the caller holds the private key. Chain validation against CF_SYSTEM_CERT_PATH is the only check.

landing_point.why: The summary names a header-forwarded client cert. This is the only place that turns on AddCertificateForwarding with a header name the caller can configure.

unverified: Main fairness problem: the published fix is an API redesign. It adds new public methods (AddOrgAndSpacePoliciesForMutualTls, AddClientCertificateForMutualTls, AddAppInstanceIdentityCertificateForMutualTls) and marks the old ones [Obsolete] without removing the header trust. Hidden tests written against the new names cannot be reached from a problem report, and the old vulnerable paths still behave the same after the fix. That is why pattern_fit is none.

Even the new AddOrgAndSpacePoliciesForMutualTls still trusts a header (X-Forwarded-Client-Cert) and relies on Gorouter stripping it (fix.diff:436-451), so the app itself never gets proof of key possession.
